description: Operator overview of an Awa job queue fleet: backlog and lag, promotion, throughput, failures, rescues, DLQ, maintenance leader and ring health. Drill into one queue with the Awa Queue Detail dashboard.

panels.title: Oldest job
panels.description: Age of the oldest available job in the worst queue. The first signal that workers are not keeping up. It does not see jobs still in scheduled/retryable that are due but not yet promoted; see Deferred jobs.

panels.title: DLQ
panels.description: Jobs currently in the dead-letter queue.

panels.title: Error rate
panels.description: failed / (completed + failed) over the last 5 minutes.

panels.title: Throughput
panels.description: Jobs completed per second, averaged over 5 minutes.

panels.title: In flight
panels.description: Jobs executing right now, across all runtimes.

panels.title: Deferred
panels.description: Jobs in scheduled or retryable state, due or not. Compare with the promotion rate in Backlog & lag: a deferred count that keeps growing while promotion is flat is jobs piling up un-promoted.

panels.title: Rescues 15m
panels.description: Jobs rescued by the maintenance leader (stale heartbeat, deadline, callback timeout) in the last 15 minutes. Anything non-zero is worth a look; see Rescues, DLQ & database retries for the kind.

panels.title: Runtimes
panels.description: Runtimes the database currently counts as alive, as reported by queue-storage-capable runtimes (largest capability group). Independent of metric label cardinality, so it stays correct when the pipeline drops per-instance labels.

panels.title: Queue lag
panels.description: Age of the oldest available job for the ten queues with the highest lag in the selected range; on queue storage, of the oldest next-to-claim job across its lanes. Click a series for the queue detail dashboard.

targets.expr: ((max by (awa_job_queue) (awa_queue_lag_seconds{awa_job_queue=~"$queue"})) and on (awa_job_queue) topk(10, max_over_time((max by (awa_job_queue) (awa_queue_lag_seconds{awa_job_queue=~"$queue"}))[$__range:$__interval] @ end()))) * on (awa_job_queue) group_left (queue_label) (label_join(max by (awa_job_queue, awa_queue_display_name) (awa_queue_info{awa_queue_display_name!=""}), "queue_label", " · ", "awa_queue_display_name", "awa_job_queue") or on (awa_job_queue) label_replace(max by (awa_job_queue) (awa_queue_lag_seconds{awa_job_queue=~"$queue"}) * 0 + 1, "queue_label", "$1", "awa_job_queue", "(.*)"))

panels.title: Deepest queues
panels.description: Total jobs across all states for the ten deepest queues in the selected range. Click a series for the queue detail dashboard.

targets.expr: ((sum by (awa_job_queue) (max by (awa_job_queue, awa_job_state) (awa_queue_depth{awa_job_queue=~"$queue"}))) and on (awa_job_queue) topk(10, max_over_time((sum by (awa_job_queue) (max by (awa_job_queue, awa_job_state) (awa_queue_depth{awa_job_queue=~"$queue"})))[$__range:$__interval] @ end())))

panels.title: Queue depth by state
panels.description: Jobs per state across the selected queues, as published by the maintenance leader. 'available' is an upper bound (enqueued minus claimed); 'running' counts materialised leases only and can under-report on queue storage.

panels.title: Deferred backlog (scheduled + retryable)
panels.description: Jobs waiting for a future run_at, for the ten queue and state series with the highest backlog in the selected range. Rising while the lag stays low means work is accumulating un-promoted rather than starving workers.

targets.expr: ((max by (awa_job_queue, awa_job_state) (awa_queue_depth{awa_job_queue=~"$queue", awa_job_state=~"scheduled|retryable"})) and on (awa_job_queue, awa_job_state) topk(10, max_over_time((max by (awa_job_queue, awa_job_state) (awa_queue_depth{awa_job_queue=~"$queue", awa_job_state=~"scheduled|retryable"}))[$__range:$__interval] @ end())))

panels.title: Promotion rate
panels.description: Jobs promoted from scheduled/retryable to available per second, by state. Not queue-scoped. Flat zero against a growing deferred backlog is a promotion stall.

panels.title: Promotion batch size p99 / duration p99
panels.description: Size and duration of promotion batches. A batch size pinned at one value while the backlog grows points at a per-batch cap; a long duration points at the database. Quantiles need AWA 0.6.13 or later; earlier versions export buckets too coarse below 5 s, so use the mean.

panels.title: Completions / failures / retries / cancellations
panels.description: Jobs per second by outcome.

panels.title: Failure ratio by queue
panels.description: failed / (completed + failed) per queue. A queue failing while others are healthy is a handler or dependency problem, not a platform one.

targets.expr: sum by (awa_job_queue) (rate(awa_job_failed_total{awa_job_queue=~"$queue"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (awa_job_queue) (rate(awa_job_completed_total{awa_job_queue=~"$queue"}[$__rate_interval])) + sum by (awa_job_queue) (rate(awa_job_failed_total{awa_job_queue=~"$queue"}[$__rate_interval])), 1e-9)

panels.title: Throughput by queue
panels.description: Completed jobs per second for the ten busiest queues in the selected range, with display names from the queue descriptor.

targets.expr: ((sum by (awa_job_queue) (rate(awa_job_completed_total{awa_job_queue=~"$queue"}[$__rate_interval]))) and on (awa_job_queue) topk(10, max_over_time((sum by (awa_job_queue) (rate(awa_job_completed_total{awa_job_queue=~"$queue"}[$__rate_interval])))[$__range:$__interval] @ end()))) * on (awa_job_queue) group_left (queue_label) (label_join(max by (awa_job_queue, awa_queue_display_name) (awa_queue_info{awa_queue_display_name!=""}), "queue_label", " · ", "awa_queue_display_name", "awa_job_queue") or on (awa_job_queue) label_replace(max by (awa_job_queue) (awa_job_completed_total{awa_job_queue=~"$queue"}) * 0 + 1, "queue_label", "$1", "awa_job_queue", "(.*)"))

panels.title: Top 10 kinds by throughput
panels.description: Completed jobs per second for the ten job kinds with the highest rate in the selected range.

targets.expr: ((sum by (awa_job_kind) (rate(awa_job_completed_total{awa_job_queue=~"$queue"}[$__rate_interval]))) and on (awa_job_kind) topk(10, max_over_time((sum by (awa_job_kind) (rate(awa_job_completed_total{awa_job_queue=~"$queue"}[$__rate_interval])))[$__range:$__interval] @ end())))

panels.title: In-flight by queue
panels.description: Executing jobs for the ten queues with the most in flight in the selected range. One queue holding most of the in-flight slots while another waits is the noisy-neighbour signature.

targets.expr: ((sum by (awa_job_queue) (awa_job_in_flight{awa_job_queue=~"$queue"})) and on (awa_job_queue) topk(10, max_over_time((sum by (awa_job_queue) (awa_job_in_flight{awa_job_queue=~"$queue"}))[$__range:$__interval] @ end())))

panels.title: Claim rate by queue
panels.description: Jobs claimed per second for the ten queues with the highest claim rate in the selected range.

targets.expr: ((sum by (awa_job_queue) (rate(awa_job_claimed_total{awa_job_queue=~"$queue"}[$__rate_interval]))) and on (awa_job_queue) topk(10, max_over_time((sum by (awa_job_queue) (rate(awa_job_claimed_total{awa_job_queue=~"$queue"}[$__rate_interval])))[$__range:$__interval] @ end())))

panels.title: Top 10 kinds by failures
panels.description: Failed jobs per second for the ten job kinds with the highest rate in the selected range.

targets.expr: ((sum by (awa_job_kind) (rate(awa_job_failed_total{awa_job_queue=~"$queue"}[$__rate_interval]))) and on (awa_job_kind) topk(10, max_over_time((sum by (awa_job_kind) (rate(awa_job_failed_total{awa_job_queue=~"$queue"}[$__rate_interval])))[$__range:$__interval] @ end())))

panels.title: Top 10 kinds by retries
panels.description: Retried jobs per second for the ten job kinds with the highest rate in the selected range.

targets.expr: ((sum by (awa_job_kind) (rate(awa_job_retried_total{awa_job_queue=~"$queue"}[$__rate_interval]))) and on (awa_job_kind) topk(10, max_over_time((sum by (awa_job_kind) (rate(awa_job_retried_total{awa_job_queue=~"$queue"}[$__rate_interval])))[$__range:$__interval] @ end())))

panels.title: Job wait time (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: Time from job creation to claim. Rising wait with steady throughput means under-provisioned workers; rising with steady workers means a producer burst.

panels.title: Job duration (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: Execution time per queue. A regression in duration usually precedes a backlog. Quantiles need AWA 0.6.13 or later; earlier versions export buckets too coarse below 5 s, so use the mean.

panels.title: Claim latency (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: Postgres dequeue query time per queue. A rise here with healthy Postgres CPU usually means contention between queues or a bloated claim path. Quantiles need AWA 0.6.13 or later; earlier versions export buckets too coarse below 5 s, so use the mean.

panels.title: Claim batch size
panels.description: Average jobs claimed per claim query.

panels.title: Wake to first claim (p95)
panels.description: Time from a dispatcher wake-up to its first claim attempt, by wake reason. Quantiles need AWA 0.6.13 or later; earlier versions export buckets too coarse below 5 s, so use the mean.

panels.title: Dispatcher wake-ups by reason
panels.description: Wake-ups per second by reason.

panels.title: Empty claims & rate-limited wakes
panels.description: Wakes that found no work despite free capacity, and wakes blocked by a rate limit. Persistent rate limiting explains a backlog with idle workers.

panels.title: Completion flush (p50 / p95)
panels.description: Time per batched completion flush. Quantiles need AWA 0.6.13 or later; earlier versions export buckets too coarse below 5 s, so use the mean.

panels.title: Maintenance rescues by kind
panels.description: Jobs rescued per interval by kind: stale heartbeat (worker died), deadline (attempt ran past its deadline) and callback timeout. Not queue-scoped.

panels.title: DLQ inflow by queue & reason
panels.description: Jobs moved to the dead-letter queue per interval. Bulk admin moves carry no queue label and only appear while the queue filter is All.

panels.title: DLQ depth by queue
panels.description: Jobs currently in the dead-letter queue.

panels.title: DLQ retried / purged
panels.description: Jobs retried out of, or purged from, the dead-letter queue per interval.

panels.title: Completion retries (deadlock / reconnect)
panels.description: Finalize transactions re-run after a Postgres deadlock abort, and retries started after the database became unavailable (connection loss, pool timeout, failover). Any sustained rate is a database-side problem. The reconnect counter exists from 0.7.

panels.title: Jobs parked for callback
panels.description: Jobs parked waiting for an external callback, per second by kind.

panels.title: Instances running maintenance
panels.description: Number of series executing maintenance branches. Healthy is 1. Zero or no data means no leader is running maintenance (promotion, rescue, rotation and prune all stop); more than 1 is a handover window or a split.

panels.title: Current maintenance leader
panels.description: Series that ran a maintenance branch in the last 5 minutes. The labels identify the leading runtime (instance, pod or service labels, depending on your pipeline).

panels.title: Branch overrun episodes
panels.description: Transitions of a branch from on-time to running past its own tick interval.

panels.title: Branch executions
panels.description: Maintenance branch executions per second.

panels.title: Branch duration p99
panels.description: Wall-clock time of each maintenance branch body. The branch loop is single-threaded, so one slow branch delays all the others.

panels.title: Rotation rate by ring + outcome
panels.description: Ring rotation attempts per second by ring (queue/lease/claim) and outcome. Healthy rings rotate on a regular cadence; pinned rings are dominated by skipped_busy.

panels.title: Rotation skip blockers (queue ring)
panels.description: What is pinning the queue ring when rotation is skipped.

panels.title: Rotation skip blocker presence p95
panels.description: p95 of the non-empty signal at the blocker when rotation is skipped. Indicates presence, not backlog magnitude.

panels.title: Prune rate by ring + outcome
panels.description: Ring prune attempts per second by outcome.

panels.title: Prune skip reasons (all rings)
panels.description: Why prune skipped an active partition.

panels.title: Rotations per minute (generation derivative)
panels.description: Per-ring rotation cadence derived from the generation gauge.

panels.title: Prune database phase latency p99
panels.description: Latency of the lock, truncate and commit phases of a destructive prune.

panels.title: Job outputs (recorded / dropped)
panels.description: Job outputs published per second by outcome, and outputs not published, by reason. A sustained schema_missing rate means a binary is running ahead of its migration.

panels.title: Job output size (p50 / p95)
panels.description: Size of published outputs in bytes of JSON text.

panels.title: Staged follow-ups (inserted / duplicate / discarded)
panels.description: Handler-staged follow-ups per second by result, and follow-ups discarded because the handler returned WaitForCallback (almost always a handler bug).

panels.title: Descriptor catalogs (summary; full tables in awa-ui)
Declared queues
panels.description: awa_queue_info is always 1; it is a label-join target. The full queue table, with pause/drain actions, lives in awa-ui.

targets.expr: max by (awa_job_queue, awa_queue_display_name, awa_queue_owner, awa_queue_tags, awa_queue_docs_url) (awa_queue_info)

panels.title: Declared job kinds
panels.description: awa_job_kind_info is always 1; it is a label-join target.

targets.expr: max by (awa_job_kind, awa_job_kind_display_name, awa_job_kind_owner, awa_job_kind_tags, awa_job_kind_docs_url) (awa_job_kind_info)

panels.title: Current storage transition state
panels.description: One-hot state/engine gauge exported by queue-storage-capable runtimes. Distinguishes steady-state operation from prepared or mixed-transition rollout windows.

panels.title: Canonical live backlog
panels.description: Jobs still live on the canonical engine during a storage transition.

panels.title: Enter mixed transition
panels.description: 1 when the transition into mixed mode is ready.

panels.title: Finalize
panels.description: 1 when the transition is ready to finalize.

panels.title: Live runtime capability counts
panels.description: Live runtimes reporting each storage capability. During a mixed rollout queue_storage rises before the routing flip and canonical_drain_only falls to zero before finalize.

list.name: datasource
list.label: Datasource
list.description: Prometheus-compatible datasource receiving awa's OTLP metrics.

list.name: filters
list.label: Filters
list.description: Optional label filters applied to every query, for example an environment, cluster, namespace or service label that your metrics pipeline attaches to awa's series.

list.name: awa_ui_url
list.label: awa-ui base URL
list.description: Base URL of the awa-ui admin site. Panels link to awa-ui for the transactional views (pause, retry, drain) these dashboards deliberately do not duplicate.

title: Awa Job Queue
